_README: Hand-labelled ground truth for the ranking regression set (#31).
Each label is a judgement made by reading the posting in tests/fixtures/postings.json
and asking one question: on a Winter 2027 co-op search out of Toronto, would this be
opened or passed over? The labels were NOT read off the scorer's output. A label that
agrees with the scorer only because it was copied from it measures nothing.
pursue     - clearly worth an evening. Must outscore every 'skip'.
skip       - clearly not. Must be outscored by every 'pursue'.
borderline - genuinely arguable. Asserted only to beat the clear skips, never
pinned against the pursues: which side of a borderline case a tuning
change lands on is the thing that is actually uncertain, and a test
that pins it fails on every honest improvement.
filtered_by: the hard-filter rule expected to cut the row before scoring. A row with
this set is never scored, so it carries no label. Naming the rule rather than just
'cut' is what makes an over-eager filter visible: if seniority starts swallowing
rows that location used to cut, the rule name changes and the test says so.
The profile these are judged against is build_profile() in tests/test_ranking.py.
Changing that profile changes every label here, so change both together.

R-0000186717.label: pursue
R-0000186717.why: The target role exactly: a Winter 2027 RBC risk internship in Toronto, asking for SQL, Excel and risk vocabulary the profile has.

R-0000187520.label: pursue
R-0000187520.why: Same shape and season -- an RBC Winter 2027 internship in Toronto. The skill match is weaker than the credit risk posting, and it should rank below it, but a Toronto co-op posting in the target term is never a skip.

R_1499218.why: The location field is a placeholder, but the description explicitly states Work Location: Wilmington, Delaware, United States of America. Outside the Toronto search.

R_1508330.label: skip
R_1508330.why: A junior Toronto role, so the filters correctly let it through -- but a contact centre representative is not an analytical position and its long description names none of the profile's skills. This is the row that catches a scorer treating 'we read it and found nothing' as 'we do not know'.

R-0000183468.why: New York. Not commutable, and the profile does not accept remote.

R260025276.why: Senior Manager -- four rungs above an intern or junior target.

R260026756.why: Bank Manager II, and in Emeryville. Seniority is checked first, so that is the rule that should name it.

R_1468577.why: Montreal. The title also carries no level marker, so seniority cannot cut it -- location is the rule that has to.

R_1499215.why: Senior Quantitative Analyst, two rungs from junior. The description also states Wilmington, but seniority is checked first.
